# Invitation concepts — generated by the METHOD.md process

Specific material (theirs, real): propagation & cuttings; pothos = heart leaf, roots in days,
the plant you cut a piece off to GIVE AWAY, she keeps everything alive; monstera = fenestration
as engineering, climbs toward light; waterline — separate above, completely merged below;
the mark is designed to MATURE over 5/10/20 years; venue is a forest (״ביער״, חדרה);
3.11.26 / כ״ג בחשון תשפ״ז; a Dutch-language side of the family; proposal barefoot in the desert.

Far domains forced against it: plant care tags, nursery labels, herbarium sheets, dichotomous
botanical keys, patent drawings, soil/strata sections, growth charts, library cards, vellum
overlays, blind deboss.

**Test applied to every idea: swap the names — does it still work? If yes, it's decoration.**

---

## A. Vellum overlay — two sheets that merge  ★ hero
Two physical layers. **Sheet 1 (cream stock):** the two plants above the waterline, apart,
each itself. **Sheet 2 (translucent vellum, laid over):** the merged root mass. Apart, each
sheet is one person. Overlaid, they become the approved mark — and you cannot tell whose root
is whose. The object *performs* the concept instead of illustrating it.
- Vellum overlays are standard in good stationery; any Israeli printer does this.
- Ties to their locked line: *"מתחת למים השורשים כבר התערבבו לגמרי"*.
- Swap test: **passes** — meaningless for a couple without the two-plants idea.

## B. Care instructions card  ★ the charming one
The invitation written as the care label for one shared plant.
`אור: עקיף, בשפע` · `השקיה: כשהאדמה יבשה` · `פורח: 3.11.26` · `גובה בבגרות: בלתי ידוע`.
Times become the care schedule. Warm, funny, unmistakably them — she is literally the one who
keeps the plants alive. Works brilliantly as the *back* of A or as the RSVP card.
- Swap test: **passes.**

## C. Herbarium sheet
The card is a mounted specimen with a real herbarium label: *Collector / Locality: יער, חדרה /
Date collected: 3.11.2026 / Accession no.* Museum-grade, restrained, a document rather than a
greeting. Exactly the Celine–Jil Sander register their brief demands.
- Swap test: passes, but weakly — the format is transferable. Needs the two species to carry it.

## D. Dichotomous botanical key
The invitation reads as a field key:
`1a. עלה לב, שלם → מיכל` / `1b. עלה מחורר, פנסטרטי → אופיר` / `2. שורשים בלתי נפרדים → ←`
Nerdy, precise, very Ophir. Risk: cold for the grandparents, and needs flawless Hebrew typography.

## E. Patent drawing
"A joined root system" — figure callouts numbering into the details (Fig. 1 = חופה, 20:30).
Monstera fenestration is *already* framed as engineering in their own text. Distinctive, cold.

## F. Front/back — above and below
Front: plants above the waterline, nothing else. Back: the root mass, with every logistic
detail set inside the root zone. Cheapest possible execution of the concept. A safe fallback
if vellum is rejected.

## G. Year zero
The mark's planned maturation (wedding → 5 → 10 → 20 yr) printed as four small marks along the
bottom edge, with the wedding one labelled *year zero*. Emotional, and it advertises that the
identity is designed to keep growing. Better as a detail inside A than as its own concept.

## H. Blind deboss roots
Roots printed in **no ink at all** — blind embossed, felt rather than seen. What's below the
surface isn't displayed. Craft decision that carries the meaning; also feeds their wax-seal /
15–20mm ambition. Combine with A or F.

---

## Discarded deliberately
- Continuous-line couple portrait — **already rejected in wedding-brand/BRIEF.md.**
- Botanical border / wreath / scattered sprigs — banned by the same brief.
- Forest / tree-root imagery — collides with their open craft note that roots must read as
  *fleshy water roots, not tree roots*.
- The living-ink icon set (rings, coupe glasses, getaway car) from ~/wedding-invitation —
  these are the exact wedding clichés wedding-brand forbids. **Conflict to resolve, not inherit.**

## Recommendation
**A as hero, B on the reverse or as the RSVP, H as the print treatment.**
One object: two sheets, two plants, one root mass you can feel but not see.

---

# Round 2 — what the online search added (far-domain only, no wedding queries)

## Herbarium sheets — /tmp/i1.png (real museum sheets, not Etsy)
Three things I had wrong in concept C:
- The **specimen is mounted off-centre** and the sheet is mostly EMPTY. The label is small,
  typed, parked in the **bottom-right corner**. Restraint is the whole look.
- Sheets carry **accession numbers, institutional stamps** (red ISOTYPE stamps), and a barcode.
- **Annotation slips accumulate over decades** — later botanists glue on a new determination
  slip without removing the old one. The sheet is a record that keeps being added to.
→ This is a direct hit on their locked "the mark matures over 5/10/20 years" idea. A herbarium
  sheet is *designed* to be re-annotated. Anniversary slips could be added to the same sheet.

## Nursery / plant care tags — /tmp/i3.png
The real horticultural language is **pictogram-driven**: sun icon with fill states (full /
partial / shade), a water-drop scale, hardiness zone, a barcode, "H 3 × W 2m" mature-size line,
and the cultivar name in inverted commas — `CAMELLIA 'FAIRY BLUSH'`.
→ Concept B gets sharper: `MICHAL × OPHIR 'חדרה'` set as a cultivar name, with a real mature-size
  line and sun/water pictograms. The die-cut pointed-stake tag shape is also a printable format.

## Blind deboss — confirmed practical (riseandshinepaper, thecuriousprintmaker)
Letterpress impression with **no ink at all**; needs **≥220gsm** stock; the image is read purely
as light and shadow and **changes with viewing angle**. Cheap in the sense that it needs no ink,
but needs a die. Confirms concept H is real, not a fantasy.
Adjacent techniques worth knowing: foil + emboss combined (relief plus reflection), and
thermochromic ink (colour changes with heat — a root mass that appears when you hold it).

## Net effect on the recommendation
Unchanged in shape, sharper in detail:
**A (vellum overlay)** hero · **B (care tag, now in real nursery-tag language)** on the reverse ·
**H (blind-deboss roots, ≥220gsm)** as the print treatment · and steal from the herbarium:
an **accession number and a corner label** instead of a centred greeting, plus the
re-annotation logic as the anniversary mechanic.

## Also possible now (new)
**Thermochromic roots** — the root mass invisible until touched, appearing from the warmth of
the hand. Literally: what's below the surface shows only when someone holds it. Gimmick risk is
real, cost is real, but it is the most on-concept novelty technique available.

---

# Round 3 — parallel search + generation (warm / celebratory registers)

Reframe that triggered this: the "Celine / not wedding stationery" rule in wedding-brand/BRIEF.md
was written about the **logo**. The invitation is a different object with a different job —
make 200 people feel invited, carry real information, live on a fridge for 8 months.
Austerity is right for a wax seal and wrong for a party.

## Searched (all far-domain, none in the wedding index) — /tmp/psheet_all.jpg
- **Risograph botanical posters** — flat overprinted inks, wild colour (pink/yellow/cobalt),
  leaves cropped hard by the frame, halftone grain. Celebratory and modern *at the same time*.
- **Matisse cut-outs** — organic leaf shapes as pure flat colour, no outline, arranged with air.
  Directly compatible with the mark: their leaves are already solid filled shapes.
- **Vintage seed packets** — dense frames, saturated litho colour, generous and gift-like.

## Generated (gemini-3-pro-image, from the approved mark) — out/G1..G3, out/gen_sheet.jpg
- **G1 — warm colour version of the mark.** Wine / gold / sage leaves, warm brown roots on
  cream. Proves the mark survives colour and immediately feels 10× warmer than the black
  version, with zero structural change. **Lowest-risk, highest-return move available.**
- **G2 — failed.** Ignored the seed-packet brief and returned a near-copy of the logo.
  (Also re-drew the MICHAL/OPHIR type, which I had asked it not to.)
- **G3 — riso two-colour.** Pink/wine + sage overprinting, plants blown up so the leaves crop
  off all four edges, roots a dense tangled overprinted mass under the waterline.
  Energetic, modern, unmistakably a celebration. The strongest new direction today.

## What this changes
The problem was never the mark — it was that I kept printing it small and black on empty paper.
Same mark, bigger, in colour, cropping off the page = a wedding invitation.
Same mark, small and black, centred = a letterhead.

Next: type over G1 and G3, with the details in the calm zone, and test at real size.
